item.text: I spotted one design gap: external code cannot safely inject a custom display with the same rules engine today. I’m tightening that by replacing the loose display-constructor hook with an explicit headless entry point that always shares the simulator’s internal rules engine.

The constructor path is safe now: both the automatic and forced-headless modes build displays with the simulator’s own rules engine. I’m running one last compile and then I’ll summarize the new headless entry points and the structural split.

Refactored the runtime so the simulation no longer depends on Swing types.

The main split is a new display boundary in [SimulationDisplay.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/SimulationDisplay.java:1) plus a UI-neutral color type in [DisplayColor.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/DisplayColor.java:1). `Simulator` now holds a `SimulationDisplay` instead of a `JFrame`-backed view, and the species palette in [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/Simulator.java:31) no longer imports `java.awt.Color`. The constructor path was also updated so `Simulator.createHeadless(...)` at [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/Simulator.java:79) always runs without instantiating Swing.

The old Swing-heavy view code was moved into [SwingSimulationView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/SwingSimulationView.java:1). [SimulatorView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/SimulatorView.java:1) is now just a small facade that selects either Swing or headless mode, and [HeadlessSimulationView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R012_module_java/HeadlessSimulationView.java:1) provides a non-GUI implementation suitable for tests or server-side runs.
